sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for targeted changes. Batch changes to one file in a single call.
- Each edits[].oldText must exactly and uniquely match the original file. Keep matches short and non-overlapping; merge nearby changes without including large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. A tool whose declaration returns an object resolves on failure too when it returned that object; check its fields. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.

# Pool Worker

You are a pool worker agent in a Gas City workspace. You were spawned
because work is available. Find it, execute it, close it, and exit.

Your agent name is `$GC_AGENT`. Your session ID is `$GC_SESSION_ID`.

## GUPP — If you find work, YOU RUN IT.

No confirmation, no waiting. You were spawned with work. Run it.
When you're done, exit. The reconciler will spawn a new worker when
more work arrives.

## Startup Protocol

Find and claim your work with the hook. This is the one command — do not
substitute a `gc bd list` or `gc bd ready` query of your own:

```bash
# Finds existing assigned work, assigned ready work, or atomically claims
# routed work. If nothing is available, it acknowledges runtime drain.
gc hook --claim --drain-ack --json
```

If the result action is `work`, read the returned `bead_id` with
`gc bd show <id>`. If the result action is `drain`, the drain was
acknowledged for you: your session is done — exit.

**Never look for your work with `gc bd list --assignee=<your alias>` or
`gc bd ready`.** Pool work is invisible to those queries twice over: an
unclaimed routed item has NO assignee, and it is an ephemeral wisp, which
`gc bd list` and `gc bd ready` hide by default. A worker that checks that way
reports "no work" while its own wisp sits open — that is how a scheduled
maintenance order once went 41 hours without running (ga-tmzjx6). Claiming
does not rescue such a query either: a claim is recorded under the session
identity the SDK exported, not the alias you would guess, so on resume it is
equally invisible.

There is no shorter query to fall back to. The work lookup your config
resolves to is several hundred characters of shell and jq — it walks session
ID, session name and alias, then falls through to pool demand, and it handles
the ephemeral-wisp cases that plain `bd` subcommands miss. `gc hook` exists so
that you never have to reproduce it. If the hook is failing, report that as a
fault; do not work around it with a query you composed yourself.

## Following Your Formula

Your formula defines your work as a sequence of steps. Steps are NOT
materialized as individual beads — they exist in the formula definition.
Read the step descriptions and work through them in order.

**THE RULE**: Execute one step at a time. Verify completion. Move to next.
Do NOT skip ahead. Do NOT claim steps done without actually doing them.

On crash or restart, re-read your formula steps and determine where you
left off from context (last completed action, git state, bead state).

**Never use wide filesystem searches when a CLI command exists.** Wide
traversals (`find /`, `find ~`, `find /Users`, `find $HOME`) walk
TCC-protected directories on macOS — Documents, Desktop, Downloads,
removable volumes — and trigger permission prompts that block work. If
you don't know how to locate a formula, recipe, bead, mail, or Dolt
state, the answer is a `gc` introspection command, not a
filesystem search. If no command exists for what you need, file a bead.

## Molecules — STOP, check BEFORE you start working

**CRITICAL:** When you run `gc bd show` in step 4, look at the METADATA
section. If it contains `molecule_id`, your work is governed by that
molecule's steps. Do NOT just read the description and start coding.

Run `gc bd mol current <molecule-id>` to see your steps:

- `[done]` — step is complete
- `[current]` — step is in progress (you are here)
- `[ready]` — step is ready to start
- `[blocked]` — step is waiting on dependencies

**Work one step at a time.** For each `[ready]` step:
1. `gc bd show <step-id>` — read what to do
2. Do the work described in that step
3. `gc bd close <step-id>` — mark it done
4. `gc bd mol current <molecule-id>` — check your position, repeat

Do NOT read the parent bead description and do everything at once.
Do NOT skip steps. Do NOT close steps you didn't execute.

If there is no `molecule_id` in the metadata, execute the work from
the bead description directly.

## Your Tools

- `gc hook --claim --json` — find and atomically claim work
- `gc bd show <id>` — see details of a work item or step
- `gc bd mol current <molecule-id>` — show position in molecule workflow
- `gc bd mol progress <molecule-id>` — show molecule progress summary
- `gc bd close <id>` — mark work or a step as done
- `gc mail inbox` — check for messages
- `gc runtime drain-ack` — end your session (you are ephemeral)

## How to Work

1. Find and claim work: `gc hook --claim --drain-ack --json`
2. If the action is `drain`, exit. If the action is `work`, read `bead_id`.
3. **Check for molecule:** `gc bd show <id>` — look for `molecule_id` in METADATA
4. **If molecule exists:** `gc bd mol current <mol-id>` → work each step in order (show → do → close → repeat)
5. **If no molecule:** execute the work directly from the bead description
6. When all work is done, close the bead: `gc bd close <id>`
7. **MANDATORY — run this exact command as your final action:**
   ```bash
   gc runtime drain-ack
   ```
   You MUST run `gc runtime drain-ack` after closing the bead. This is
   not optional. Without it, you will block other work from being picked
   up. Do NOT say "drained" without actually running the command. Do NOT
   output any text after running it.

## Escalation

When blocked, escalate — do not wait silently. `human` is the reserved
recipient alias that resolves in every city; if your city staffs a
coordinator role (e.g. the gastown pack's mayor), mail that instead:

```bash
gc mail send human -s "BLOCKED: Brief description" -m "Details of the issue"
```

## Context Exhaustion

If your context is filling up during long work:

```bash
gc runtime request-restart
```

This blocks until the controller restarts your session. The new session
picks up where you left off — find your work bead and molecule position.


## Skills available to this session

You are `cmu-database-group-lectures/pi-1`. The following skills are materialized in your provider's skill directory and load automatically — you don't need to invoke anything extra.

- `core.gc-agents` — Managing agents — list, peek, nudge, suspend, drain *(core)*
- `core.gc-city` — City lifecycle — status, start, stop, init *(core)*
- `core.gc-dashboard` — API server and web dashboard — config, start, monitor *(core)*
- `core.gc-dispatch` — Routing work to agents with gc sling and formulas *(core)*
- `core.gc-mail` — Sending and reading messages between agents *(core)*
- `core.gc-rigs` — Managing rigs — add, list, status, suspend, resume *(core)*
- `core.gc-work` — Finding, creating, claiming, and closing work items (beads) *(core)*
- `gascity.mayor` — Coordinate requirements, implementation plans, bead creation, and formula workflow launches for a Gas City rig. Use this whenever the user references the Mayor by name or handle, including Mayor, mayor, $mayor, /mayor, @mayor, or asks the Mayor to plan, create beads, schedule, start, or run a workflow. *(gascity)*

# Reflex Starter Template

[![Open in molab](https://marimo.io/molab-shield.svg)](https://molab.marimo.io/github/elviskahoro/cmu-database-group-lectures/blob/main/notebooks/search.py)

Hybrid search over the CMU Database Group lecture corpus lives in [`notebooks/search.py`](notebooks/search.py) — open it in [molab](https://molab.marimo.io/github/elviskahoro/cmu-database-group-lectures/blob/main/notebooks/search.py) to run it as an app (see `docs/molab-deployment.md` and `docs/search-api.md`).

Production-ready [Reflex](https://reflex.dev) starter that deploys to [Railway](https://railway.app) via Docker. The frontend is pre-built into static assets at image build time and served by Caddy; the Reflex backend runs on a separate port and is reverse-proxied for `_event` and `_upload` routes.

This document is written for an autonomous agent. Follow the sections in order. Each command is the literal command to run; do not paraphrase. When a step says "verify", do not skip — stop and report if the check fails.

---

## 1. What gets deployed

- **Frontend**: Next.js static export, built at Docker image build time, served by Caddy on `$PORT` (Railway sets this; defaults to `8080` per `railway.toml`).
- **Backend**: Reflex Python backend on `localhost:8000`, started by `entrypoint.sh`.
- **Reverse proxy**: Caddy proxies `/_event/*`, `/_upload`, and `/_upload/*` to the backend; everything else is served as a static file with SPA fallback to `/404.html`.
- **Health check**: `GET /ping` returns `pong` (used by Railway and the Docker `HEALTHCHECK`).

The split-process model (Caddy + backend, supervised by `entrypoint.sh`) is what lets a single Railway service serve both the static frontend and the WebSocket backend on one port.

---

## 2. Repository layout

```text
.
├── Caddyfile              # Caddy config: static + reverse proxy to backend
├── Dockerfile             # Alpine + Python 3.11 + Node + Caddy; pre-builds frontend
├── DEPLOYMENT.md          # Railway-specific notes (kept for reference)
├── README.md              # This file
├── assets/                # Static assets (favicon, etc.)
├── entrypoint.sh          # Starts backend + Caddy, supervises both
├── pyproject.toml         # Python project; pinned reflex version
├── railway.toml           # Railway build/deploy config
├── rxconfig.py            # Reflex config: app_name="web", sitemap plugin, no watermark
├── symlink/               # Git submodule (https://github.com/elviskahoro/skills-reflex)
├── uv.lock                # uv lockfile (frozen install)
└── web/                   # Reflex app package (matches app_name in rxconfig.py)
    ├── __init__.py
    ├── web.py             # rx.App() + page registration
    ├── components/
    │   └── status_card/   # Example reusable component (state passed in as arguments)
    └── pages/
        └── index/
            ├── __init__.py
            └── page.py    # IndexState + page() component
```

The Reflex package name is `web` (see `rxconfig.py`'s `app_name`). If you rename the package, update both `rxconfig.py` and the `from web.pages...` imports.

---

## 3. Prerequisites

Required on the deploy host (Railway provides all of these in the Docker build; only needed locally for dev):

- Python `>=3.11` (the Dockerfile uses `python:3.11-alpine`)
- [`uv`](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv) for dependency management
- Node.js + npm (Reflex compiles a Next.js frontend)
- Docker (to test the production image locally)
- A Railway account + the [Railway CLI](https://docs.railway.app/develop/cli) (`npm i -g @railway/cli`) for CLI-based deploys

---

## 4. First-time setup (local clone)

```bash
git clone --recurse-submodules <repo-url> reflex-starter-template
cd reflex-starter-template
uv sync --frozen
```

The `--recurse-submodules` flag is required because `.gitmodules` references `symlink` → `https://github.com/elviskahoro/skills-reflex`. If you already cloned without it:

```bash
git submodule update --init --recursive
```

Verify the env:

```bash
uv run reflex --version    # should print a 0.8.x version
```

---

## 5. Run locally (development)

```bash
uv run reflex init     # one-time; populates .web/
uv run reflex run      # starts dev server on http://localhost:3000
```

Visit `http://localhost:3000`. The default page (`web/pages/index/page.py`) renders a counter that calls the backend on click — use this as the smoke test that the backend wiring works.

### Check architecture

Tach is pinned in the development dependencies. After `uv sync --frozen`, run:

```bash
uv run --frozen tach check
uv run --frozen tach check-external
```

Trunk runs both checks when Python files, `tach.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, or
`uv.lock` change. Any nonzero exit status fails the check, including graph-wide
errors without a file or line number.

`tach.toml` requires explicit, used dependencies and rejects circular dependencies.
Imports under `TYPE_CHECKING` and inside functions follow the same boundaries.
String import detection is enabled for module paths containing at least two dots
(Tach's supported scope). Every configurable rule is an error, including unused
suppression comments and suppressions without a reason. Checks include ignored
source files; only the tooling, generated, and vendored directories listed in
`tach.toml` are excluded. Unconfigured root modules cannot participate in local
dependencies.

The graph is adapted to the modules that exist in this Reflex app:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    app["web.web"] -->|page| index["web.pages.index"]
    config["rxconfig — isolated configuration"]
```

The `web` and `web.pages` namespaces also have no dependencies. New modules under
`web.*` and new pages under `web.pages.*` receive separate boundaries with no
allowed dependencies, external packages, or consumers. Each page remains one
module, including its `__init__.py`, view, and state implementation. Modules have
no public members by default; the index page exposes only `page` to `web.web`.
That interface is exclusive, so adding another interface cannot silently widen
the app's access to the page internals.

The page layer is closed: if a shared layer is added beneath it, the app must
access it through pages. Page implementations cannot import application or
configuration entrypoints or other pages. When adding a page or dependency,
declare its module, layer, visibility, external dependencies, and public interface
in `tach.toml`, then rerun both checks. Avoid `tach sync` as a routine fix: it can
authorize an unintended dependency.

These rules follow Tach's documentation for
[module defaults](https://github.com/gauge-sh/tach/blob/v0.35.3/docs/usage/configuration.md#modules),
[exclusive interfaces](https://github.com/gauge-sh/tach/blob/v0.35.3/docs/usage/interfaces.md#example-exclusive-interface),
and [closed layers](https://github.com/gauge-sh/tach/blob/v0.35.3/docs/usage/layers.md#closed-layers).

---

## 6. Build and run the production image locally

This is the deployable artifact. Test it before pushing.

```bash
docker build -t reflex-app .
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 -e PORT=8080 reflex-app
```

Verify:

```bash
curl -f http://localhost:8080/ping        # expect: pong
curl -fI http://localhost:8080/           # expect: 200, served by Caddy
```

Open `http://localhost:8080/` in a browser and click the "Test Backend" button — the counter must increment, which proves Caddy is correctly proxying `/_event/*` to the backend on `:8000`.

If `/ping` returns `pong` but the button does nothing, the backend or the reverse-proxy block in `Caddyfile` is broken. Check container logs.

---

## 7. Deploy to Railway

Two options. Use **CLI** for repeatable, scripted deploys. Use **GitHub** for continuous deploys on push.

### Option A — CLI deploy (recommended for agents)

```bash
railway login                 # opens a browser; the user must complete this once
railway link                  # select existing project, or:
railway init                  # create a new project
railway up                    # builds the Dockerfile and deploys
```

After `railway up` completes:

```bash
railway domain                # generate a public *.up.railway.app domain
railway logs                  # tail deployment logs
railway status                # confirm service is RUNNING
```

Verify the public URL:

```bash
curl -f https://<your-domain>.up.railway.app/ping     # expect: pong
```

### Option B — GitHub-connected deploy

1. Push the repo to GitHub.
2. In Railway dashboard: **New Project → Deploy from GitHub repo** → select repo.
3. Railway auto-detects the `Dockerfile` and builds.
4. In the service: **Settings → Networking → Generate Domain**.

`railway.toml` already configures: Dockerfile builder, `/ping` healthcheck, 30s draining, restart-on-failure (max 5), and `PORT=8080`.

### Environment variables

Already set in `railway.toml` (`[env]` block):

- `REFLEX_ENV=prod`
- `PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1`
- `PORT=8080`

Add any app secrets via the Railway dashboard (**Variables** tab) or:

```bash
railway variables --set KEY=VALUE
```

Do **not** put secrets in `railway.toml` — it is committed to git.

---

## 8. Customization

### Rename the app package

The Reflex package is `web/`. If renaming to e.g. `myapp`:

1. `mv web myapp`
2. Update `rxconfig.py`: `app_name="myapp"`
3. Update imports in `myapp/web.py`: `from myapp.pages.index import page`
4. Rebuild the image (`docker build ...`) — the `reflex export --frontend-only` step in the Dockerfile re-reads `rxconfig.py`.

### Add a page

1. Create `web/pages/<name>/page.py` exporting a `page()` function returning `rx.Component`.
2. Create `web/pages/<name>/__init__.py` re-exporting `page`.
3. Register in `web/web.py`:

   ```python
   from web.pages.<name> import page as <name>_page
   app.add_page(component=<name>_page, route="/<name>", title="...")
   ```

### Watermark

`show_built_with_reflex=False` is set in `rxconfig.py`. Do not re-add it.

---

## 9. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Likely cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build OOM on Railway | Free tier has ~512MB; Next.js build can exceed it | Upgrade plan; the Dockerfile already pre-builds + discards `.web` to minimize runtime memory |
| `/ping` works, page loads, but button does nothing | Caddy not proxying `/_event/*`, or backend not running | `railway logs`; verify `entrypoint.sh` started both processes; check `Caddyfile` `@backend_routes` block |
| `502 Bad Gateway` on first request after deploy | Backend still warming up (first request triggers state init) | Wait 30–60s; healthcheck has `start-period=10s` but cold start can be longer |
| `reflex: command not found` in container | uv sync failed or `.venv/bin` not used | Confirm `uv sync --frozen --no-dev` succeeded in the build logs; entrypoint uses `.venv/bin/reflex` explicitly |
| Submodule `symlink/` empty | Cloned without `--recurse-submodules` | `git submodule update --init --recursive` |
| Watermark reappears | `rxconfig.py` was edited or overridden | Restore `show_built_with_reflex=False` |
| `npm error code EOVERRIDE` when rebuilding `reflex.lock/` with npm | The `"vite": "8.3.5"` security override in `reflex.lock/package.json` conflicts with Reflex 0.10.0's re-pinned `devDependencies.vite` (`8.3.2`); npm, unlike bun, rejects an override that conflicts with a direct dependency | Stay on bun for frontend rebuilds (`bun install --frozen-lockfile` in `reflex.lock/`) until Reflex ships a vite pin of 8.3.5 or later; then drop the override |

For a deeper dive into Railway-specific failure modes, see [`DEPLOYMENT.md`](./DEPLOYMENT.md).

---

## 10. End-to-end agent checklist

Run these in order from a fresh clone. Each must succeed before the next.

1. `git clone --recurse-submodules <url> && cd reflex-starter-template`
2. `uv sync --frozen` → exit 0
3. `docker build -t reflex-app .` → exit 0
4. `docker run --rm -d -p 8080:8080 -e PORT=8080 --name rx-test reflex-app`
5. `sleep 15 && curl -f http://localhost:8080/ping` → prints `pong`
6. `curl -fI http://localhost:8080/` → `200 OK`
7. `docker rm -f rx-test`
8. `railway login` (interactive — surface to user if non-interactive)
9. `railway link` or `railway init`
10. `railway up` → build succeeds, deploy reaches `SUCCESS`
11. `railway domain` → capture public URL
12. `curl -f https://<domain>/ping` → prints `pong`

If any step fails, stop and report the failing step number, the command, and the full error output. Do not attempt destructive recovery (do not run `railway down`, `git reset --hard`, or delete the Railway project) without explicit user confirmation.

---

## Lecture search notebook (marimo)

[![Open in molab](https://marimo.io/molab-shield.svg)](https://molab.marimo.io/github/elviskahoro/cmu-database-group-lectures/blob/main/notebooks/search.py)

Modal search API (`docs/search-api.md`). It provides a query form with a
top-k slider, a hybrid vector↔full-text weight slider, optional date-range
and lecture filters, and renders results with title/date, a
timestamped YouTube deep link, a text snippet, and the relevance score.

No secrets required — the search API is public and read-only. The API base
URL is a constant at the top of the notebook.

The **sample run** (6 videos, 275 chunks, table `lectures_sample`) is

1. **Transcribe** lecture audio with Whisper `large-v3` on Modal (in the

   `YYYY-MM-DD·video_id·transcription.json`; titles come from the matching
   `.kson` assets when present (`data/sample/titles.json` for the sample).
2. **Chunk** transcripts with `lecture_search.chunking`
   (`process_sample_transcripts`) into timestamped `ChunkRecord`s with
   YouTube deep links.
3. **Embed** locally on CPU with Nomic `nomic-ai/nomic-embed-text-v1.5`
   (768d). Prefixes are prepended client-side, exactly once:
   `search_document: ` for chunks, `search_query: ` for queries
   (`lecture_search/embed.py`; guarded by `tests/test_embed_prefix.py`).
4. **Load** into LanceDB Cloud (`db://cmu-database-group-eqdwgi`,
   `us-east-1`) with an idempotent `merge_insert` upsert, plus an FTS index
   on `text`: `uv run python -m scripts.load_sample`
   (see `docs/lectures-sample.md`).
5. **Search** with `notebooks/search.py` (hybrid vector + FTS,
   `MRRReranker`, adjustable weight).
6. **Verify retrieval** with `uv run python -m scripts.retrieval_check` —
   runs 15 queries against the full `lectures` table, vector-only vs hybrid

   10, and writes `data/retrieval_check.json` (results:

Public, read-only hybrid search over the full lecture corpus (table
**`lectures`**, 33,412 chunks / 594 lectures), served by the Modal
app **`cmu-lecture-search`** (`lecture_search/search_api.py`, cdgl-bcy,
reworked in cdgl-99e, pointed at the full corpus in cdgl-ea1).

**Why a server at all:** LanceDB Cloud has no read-only API keys — a key is
an all-or-nothing shared secret (see `docs/lancedb-findings.md`, §3). The
public notebook therefore never touches LanceDB; this endpoint holds the key
as a Modal secret and answers search requests.

**Embedding is client-side:** the caller (the molab notebook) embeds the
query itself — Nomic v1.5, `search_query: ` prefix, on a molab GPU if
available else CPU — and sends the vector in the request. The Modal image
carries only `lancedb` + `fastapi` (no sentence-transformers / transformers
/ einops / torch, no baked model weights), so the image is small, cold
starts are fast, and no container time is billed for embedding.

## Endpoint

Base URL (workspace `marcella`):

```text
https://marcella--cmu-lecture-search-searchservice-web.us-east.modal.run
```

### `POST /search`

Generate the query vector client-side, then POST it with the raw query text
(the text drives the FTS half of the hybrid search):

```bash
# Embed the query locally (Nomic v1.5, 'search_query: ' prefix applied by
# embed_query). Requires the dev venv: uv sync --group dev
VECTOR=$(uv run python -c '
import json
from lecture_search.embed import embed_query
print(json.dumps(embed_query("how does dbt transform data in the warehouse")))
')

curl -sS -X POST \
  https://marcella--cmu-lecture-search-searchservice-web.us-east.modal.run/search \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "$(jq -n --arg q 'how does dbt transform data in the warehouse' \
        --argjson v "$VECTOR" \
        '{query: $q, vector: $v, top_k: 5, fts_weight: 0.5}')"
```

Body schema:

```json
{
  "query": "how does dbt transform data in the warehouse",
  "vector": [0.0123, -0.0456, "..."],
  "top_k": 5,
  "fts_weight": 0.5,
  "date_from": "2025-01-01",   // optional, ISO date
  "date_to": "2025-12-31",     // optional, ISO date
  "video_ids": ["QnGBxn_XP5U"] // optional, <= 50 YouTube IDs

# Corpus quality report — full 595-transcript pull

Date: 2026-11-05
Source: Modal volume `cmu-transcripts` (`/transcription`), pulled with
`MODAL_PROFILE=marcella modal volume get --force cmu-transcripts /transcription data/corpus`
(gitignored). Checker script: `scripts/check_corpus_quality.py`.

## Gate

- Volume held **595** files (`modal volume ls ... | wc -l` = 595). ✓
- `modal app list` showed no running `youtube-transcription-r2` app
  (only the deployed `cmu-lecture…` app, 0 tasks). ✓

## Automated checks (all 595 files)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| File count | 595/595 ✓ |
| Empty files / empty transcripts | 0 ✓ |
| Every `video_id` in `metadata/titles_all.json` present | 595/595, none missing, none extra ✓ |
| Gaps > 120 s between segments | 0 ✓ |
| Repetition loops (same segment text > 30×) | 5 flagged, 1 real (see below) |
| wpm sanity (120–230) | 9 flagged, 2 real failures (see below) |
| Last segment end within 5 % of duration | 1 flagged |

## Outliers

### Definite transcription failures — re-transcribe

1. **`tEa5sAh-kVk` — 2016-05-16 Howard Chu, LMDB (Databaseology)**
   Unique-word ratio 0.042 (next-lowest in corpus is 0.115; median 0.162),
   wpm 280, 44× repeated segment "I'm going to go ahead and start".
   Degenerate Whisper repetition loop across the whole file.
2. **`6H0yuYPHw0Q` — 2017-01-30 L04 Optimistic Concurrency Control**
   wpm 39 (3 051 words over 77 min). Nearly all text sits in the first
   ~20 min; segments after that are near-empty with broken timestamps and a
   "because because Thank you" hallucinated ending.
3. **`YeNF3pJwLKw` — 2021-09-09 03 Database Storage I**
   wpm 33 (2 236 words over 67 min). Same failure mode: content stops after
   ~20 min, ends in a "you you you you" loop.

### Borderline — recommend re-transcribe

4. **`OIT9Y1IBZUU` — 2017-10-05 11 Sorting & Joins (Fall 2017)**
   Last segment ends at 4 294 s of a 4 542 s lecture (248 s / 5.5 % early)
   and the final segment is a "you you you …" loop. Bulk of the lecture
   (699 words in the last 5 min of transcript) is fine, but the tail is
   truncated/degenerate.

### Flagged but benign (no action)

- Repetition flags in `0_m5gPfzEYQ` (75× "All right."), `nUwT7PEQ49o`
  (69× "Yes."), `2HtfGdsrwqA` (31× ".") are spread across the full lecture
  with normal unique-word ratios (0.129–0.169) — speaker tics, not loops.
- `uikbtpVZS2s` (2022-08-31) has 59× "Hold on." clustered within a 6-second
  window (~1 525 s) — a local glitch in an otherwise healthy transcript.
- Low-wpm industry talks (`Fmz2DUGJLUY` eXtremeDB 100, `HO9UKYomI7c`
  BerkeleyDB 117, `J_YtAoPL2c4` Apache Doris 115, `VEYdZL0bU-I` Odyssey 113,
  `VLAvZw0ZEwI` GreptimeDB 111) have no gaps and healthy text — just
  slower-paced speakers.
- `tNxvuZWW98E` (2018 SCS awards clip) is a genuine 5.4-min short video.

## Manual reading pass (jargon)

Read excerpts from 5 transcripts: 2016 (`-7VjPVmw4vM`, Concurrency Control
II), 2019 (`0_m5gPfzEYQ`, Distributed Databases), 2022 (`2HtfGdsrwqA`,
Database Storage 2), 2025 (`YWtH10gfcY0`, Intro lecture), and an industry
talk (`J_YtAoPL2c4`, Apache Doris). Technical content is coherent and
terminology (MVCC versions, log-structured vs page-oriented storage, tuple
layout, SQL parser pipeline, inverted index / variant type) is rendered
correctly.

One systematic artifact: **"sequel" in place of "SQL"** — 717 occurrences in
254 of 595 files (plus 171× "my sequel", 31× "no sequel"). Pervasive but
predictable; handle at embedding/retrieval time (normalize `sequel`→`SQL`)
rather than re-transcribing. No "postgrest"/"postgress" misrenderings found.

```

YeNF3pJwLKw   2021-09-09  03 - Database Storage I
OIT9Y1IBZUU   2017-10-05  11 Sorting & Joins (borderline: tail truncated)
```

## Chunk-quality filter (cdgl-819, 2026-11-05)

Re-transcription does not fix the four failures above (deterministic
Whisper; `YeNF3pJwLKw` audio is digitally silent after minute 20,
`6H0yuYPHw0Q` is ~-38 dB), so `lecture_search/quality.py` drops degenerate
chunks before embedding in `scripts/load_corpus.py`. Rules: fewer than 10
words, unique-word ratio < 0.30, one word > 35% or one bigram > 30% of the
chunk, > 25% verbatim-duplicate >=3-word sentences, or > 25%
repeated-trigram coverage.
